name: Abū Muʿāwiya Shaybān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Tamīmī al-Naḥwī
summary: Qurʾān reader, transmitter of ḥadīth and early grammarian, client of Tamīm, who taught the children of the ʿAbbāsid Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī and moved from Kufa to Baghdad, where he died in 164/781.
bio: Shaybān was a client of the Banū Tamīm and tutor to the children of Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn al-Anbārī calls him a Qurʾān reader, a transmitter of ḥadīth and one of the early grammarians: he lived for a time in Kufa and then moved to Baghdad, transmitting from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, while ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī and others transmitted from him.
His name al-Naḥwī was disputed: al-ʿAskarī held that it refers not to grammar but to Naḥw ibn Shums, a clan of al-Azd, a point Ibn al-Anbārī discusses at length. He died in Baghdad in 164/781.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 38–41
